94357.q: What do you draw in a circuit diagram instead of real pictures of the parts?
94357.e: In a circuit diagram, each component has a simple symbol. That way you can draw a circuit quickly.
94357.m: A circuit diagram shows components as simple symbols.

94358.q: How does a lamp shine with an almost flat battery?
94358.e: An almost flat battery only supplies a little energy. That is why the lamp shines more faintly.
94358.m: With an almost flat battery, the lamp shines faintly.

94359.q: What does an electric bell do when the circuit is closed?
94359.e: When current flows through the bell, a small hammer strikes a bell. That makes the ringing sound.
94359.m: A bell rings when current flows.

94360.q: What is a cable called that you use to connect a device to a socket further away?
94360.e: An extension cable has a plug at one end and a socket at the other. That way the electricity reaches further.
94360.m: An extension cable takes electricity further away.

94361.q: Why shouldn't you lay a cable under a carpet?
a: It can be damaged and get hot
94361.e: Under the carpet the cable gets stepped on and can break. Also, the heat can't escape, which is dangerous.

94362.q: What do you do with a cable reel before you plug in a powerful device?
a: You put it in the sun
You tie it in a knot
94362.e: In a cable reel that is still wound up, the cable can get very hot. That is why you unroll it completely.
94362.m: Unroll a cable reel completely before using it.

94363.q: What are the thick lines that run across the country high up on big pylons called?
94363.e: High-voltage power lines carry electricity from the power stations over long distances. They hang high up on pylons.
94363.m: High-voltage lines carry electricity over long distances.

94364.q: Where are many power cables in towns and cities?
94364.e: In towns, power cables are usually laid in the ground. There they are protected and don't get in the way.
94364.m: In towns, power cables are often in the ground.

94365.q: Why do the wires in a power cable have different coloured coverings?
a: So that you can tell them apart
So that they shine more nicely
So that animals don't eat them
94365.e: Each colour shows what a wire is for. That way the electrician can connect the wires correctly.
94365.m: The colours of the wires help to connect them correctly.

94366.q: What colour is the covering of the protective earth wire?
94366.e: The protective earth wire is striped yellow and green. If there is a fault, it carries the current away safely.
94366.m: The earth wire in a cable is yellow-green.

94367.q: Why is the inside of a power cable often made of many thin wires?
a: So that it is more colourful
94367.e: Many thin wires together are easy to bend. A single thick wire would be stiff and could break.
94367.m: Many thin wires make a cable flexible.

94368.q: What is the cable you use to charge a mobile phone called?
94368.e: Through the charging cable, electricity flows from the socket into the phone's battery. You usually also need a charger plug.
94368.m: You charge a mobile phone with a charging cable.

94369.q: What is a switch called that only lets current flow while you press it, as with a doorbell?
94369.e: A push button only closes the circuit while you press it. When you let go, the circuit is open again.
94369.m: A push button only works while you press it.

94370.q: What is a switch that lets you make the light brighter or dimmer called?
94370.e: With a dimmer you can adjust the brightness of a lamp smoothly. The word comes from “dim”.
94370.m: With a dimmer you adjust the brightness.

94371.q: Why does the light on the staircase often go off by itself after a while?
a: A timer switch turns it off
94371.e: Many staircases have a timer switch. It turns the light off after a few minutes and so saves electricity.
94371.m: A timer switch turns the light off by itself.

94372.q: What switches on an outdoor light when someone walks past?
94372.e: A motion sensor notices when someone moves. Then it switches the light on for a short time.
94372.m: A motion sensor switches on the light when something moves.

94373.q: What is the red switch you use to stop a machine immediately in an emergency called?
94373.e: The emergency stop button is usually red on a yellow background. Pressing it stops the machine immediately.
94373.m: The emergency stop button stops a machine immediately.

94374.q: What does the symbol “0” on a switch mean?
94374.e: On many devices, “I” stands for on and “0” for off. When the switch is at “0”, no current flows.
94374.m: The zero on a switch means off.

94375.q: Two switches are one after the other in the same circuit. One is open. What does the lamp do?
94375.e: When the switches are connected one after the other, the current has to flow through both. If one is open, the path is broken.
94375.m: Connected in series, all switches must be closed.

94376.q: What is the small switch in the middle of the cable of a floor lamp called?
94376.e: On many floor and table lamps, the switch is right in the cable. It is called an inline switch.
94376.m: An inline switch sits in the lamp's cable.

94377.q: What lights up in an incandescent light bulb?
94377.e: In an incandescent bulb, current flows through a thin wire. The wire gets so hot that it glows brightly.
94377.m: In a light bulb, a thin wire glows.

94378.q: Which metal is the filament of a light bulb made of?
94378.e: Tungsten only melts at a very high temperature. That is why it can stand the strong glowing.
94378.m: The filament is made of tungsten.

94379.q: Which inventor made the light bulb practical for everyday use around 1880?
94379.e: The American Thomas Edison improved the light bulb so that it lasted a long time. After that it was used in many homes.
94379.m: Thomas Edison made the light bulb well known.

94380.q: Why shouldn't you touch a light bulb that has just been on?
94380.e: A light bulb gets very hot when it is shining. You can burn your fingers on it.
94380.m: A light bulb that is on is hot.

94381.q: What do you say when a light bulb stops working because its wire has broken?
94381.e: Over time the filament gets thinner and breaks. Then people say the bulb has blown.
94381.m: If the filament breaks, the bulb has blown.

94382.q: What is the part of a light fitting that you screw the bulb into called?
94382.e: The socket holds the bulb firmly and connects it to the electricity. You screw the bulb in by its thread.
94382.m: The light bulb is screwed into the socket.

94383.q: What is the round outer part of a light bulb made of?
94383.e: The outer part of a light bulb is a glass bulb. The light shines out through the glass.
94383.m: The outer part of a light bulb is made of glass.

94384.q: Why doesn't the filament burn up straight away inside the glass bulb?
a: There is no oxygen in the bulb
The wire is made of wood
94384.e: Burning needs oxygen. Inside the glass bulb there is no air, or only a gas without oxygen.
94384.m: Without oxygen, the filament doesn't burn up.

94385.q: What do you do first before changing a light bulb?
94385.e: When changing a bulb, you touch parts that may carry electricity. That is why you switch off the electricity first.
94385.m: Switch off the electricity before changing a bulb.

94386.q: What does the abbreviation LED stand for?
94386.e: LED is short for “light-emitting diode”. It is a tiny electronic part that gives off light.

94387.q: How long does an LED lamp last compared with an incandescent bulb?
94387.e: LED lamps last for many years, much longer than incandescent bulbs. That is why you rarely need to change them.
94387.m: LED lamps last much longer than incandescent bulbs.

94388.q: Does an LED get as hot as an incandescent bulb when it shines?
a: Yes, it gets just as hot
94388.e: An LED turns electricity mainly into light and only a little heat. That is why it gets much less hot.
94388.m: An LED stays fairly cool when it shines.

94389.q: What happens if you connect an LED to a battery the wrong way round?
94389.e: A diode only lets current through in one direction. The wrong way round, no current flows and it stays dark.
94389.m: An LED only lights up the right way round.

94390.q: Which leg of an LED is connected to the positive terminal?
94390.e: A simple LED has two little legs. The longer one goes to the positive terminal, the shorter one to the negative terminal.
94390.m: The long leg of the LED goes to plus.

94391.q: What does a small glowing LED light on a device often show?
94391.e: Many devices have a small indicator light. When it is on, the device is switched on or charging.
94391.m: A small light often shows that a device is on.

94392.q: How big is a single LED usually?
94392.e: LEDs are often only a few millimetres in size. That is why lots of them fit into a lamp or a screen.

94393.q: What are the pixels of many big scoreboards in stadiums made of?
94393.e: Big scoreboards are made of thousands of small LEDs. Together their dots of light make pictures and numbers.
94393.m: Big scoreboards are made of lots of LEDs.

94394.q: Which sign marks the positive terminal of a battery?
94394.e: The positive terminal has the plus sign. That way you know which way round the battery goes.
94394.m: The positive terminal has a plus sign.

94395.q: Which end of a round AA battery is the positive terminal?
a: The end with the small bump
94395.e: On round batteries, the positive terminal has a small bump. The flat end is the negative terminal.
94395.m: The bump on the battery is the positive terminal.

94396.q: How many terminals does a battery have?
94396.e: Every battery has a positive and a negative terminal. Current only flows when both are connected through a circuit.

94397.q: What do the signs + and − in the battery compartment of a device show?
a: How to put the battery in
94397.e: Plus and minus are marked in the battery compartment. The terminals of the battery must match them exactly.
94397.m: The signs in the battery compartment show the right direction.

94398.q: What often happens if a battery in a torch is the wrong way round?
94398.e: If the batteries are the wrong way round, plus and minus don't match up. Then no current flows through the lamp.
94398.m: Batteries put in the wrong way round leave the lamp dark.

94399.q: What colour is the cable for the positive terminal often, for example in a car?
94399.e: In a car, the cable for the positive terminal is usually red. The cable for the negative terminal is often black.
94399.m: Plus is often red and minus often black.

94400.q: How many volts does an ordinary car battery have?
94400.e: Most cars have a 12-volt battery. It supplies, for example, the electricity to start the engine.
94400.m: A car battery usually has 12 volts.

94401.q: What happens if you connect the positive and negative terminals of a battery directly with a wire?
a: The wire and battery get hot
94401.e: This is called a short circuit. A lot of current flows, and the wire and battery get hot. That is why you should never do it.
94401.m: A short circuit makes the wire and battery hot.

94402.q: Does a dry wooden spoon conduct electricity?
a: Yes, just as well as metal
Yes, but only a thick spoon
94402.e: Dry wood hardly lets electricity through. That is why wood is called an insulator.

94403.q: Does a metal spoon conduct electricity?
94403.e: Metals let electricity through well. So a metal spoon is a conductor.

94404.q: Which of these objects is an insulator?
94404.e: A rubber (eraser) is made of rubber or plastic. These materials don't conduct electricity; the other things are made of metal.

94405.q: Which of these objects conducts electricity?
94405.e: A paper clip is made of metal and conducts electricity. Rubber, wood and glass are insulators.
94405.m: A metal paper clip conducts electricity.

94406.q: Is glass a conductor or an insulator?
94406.e: Glass doesn't let electricity through. That is why glass is an insulator.

94407.q: Does the human body conduct electricity?
a: Yes, that is why electricity is dangerous
94407.e: The body contains a lot of water with salts, so it conducts electricity. That is why an electric shock can be dangerous.

94408.q: Does dry air normally conduct electricity?
94408.e: Dry air is normally an insulator. Only at a very high voltage, such as with lightning, can electricity jump through the air.

94409.q: Why do power lines hang from parts made of glass or porcelain?
a: So that no electricity flows into the pylon
So that the line looks nicer
So that birds can nest there
94409.e: Glass and porcelain are insulators. They hold the line in place without electricity flowing into the pylon.
94409.m: Porcelain parts keep electricity away from the pylon.

94410.q: Which materials conduct electricity especially well?
94410.e: All metals conduct electricity, and some do so especially well. That is why wires are made of metal.

94411.q: What colour is a freshly polished piece of copper?
94411.e: Copper is a metal with a reddish-brown colour. That makes it easy to recognise.

94412.q: What colour does a copper roof turn after many years outdoors?
94412.e: Copper slowly reacts with air and rain. A green layer forms that protects the metal.
94412.m: Copper roofs turn green over time.

94413.q: Which famous statue in New York is made of copper on the outside and is therefore green?
94413.e: The Statue of Liberty is covered with thin copper sheets. Over time they turned green.
94413.m: The Statue of Liberty is made of copper and so it is green.

94414.q: What is the chemical symbol for copper?
94414.e: The symbol Cu comes from the Latin word “cuprum”. That is the Latin name for copper.
94414.m: The symbol for copper is Cu.

94415.q: Which metal conducts electricity even better than copper but is much more expensive?
94415.e: Silver conducts electricity best of all. Because it is expensive, copper is usually used for cables.
94415.m: Silver conducts even better than copper.

94416.q: What is the golden-yellow mixture of copper and zinc that trumpets are often made of called?
94416.e: Brass is mainly made of copper and zinc. It shines golden yellow and is used for wind instruments and door handles.
94416.m: Brass is a mixture of copper and zinc.

94417.q: Which mixture of copper and tin has been used for bells for a long time?
94417.e: Bronze is made of copper and tin. Bronze bells sound beautiful and last a very long time.
94417.m: Bronze is a mixture of copper and tin.

94418.q: Why do some saucepans have a copper base?
94418.e: Copper conducts not only electricity but also heat very well. That is why the pan heats up quickly and evenly.

94419.q: What is copper obtained from in mines?
94419.e: Copper is found in certain rocks called copper ores. In mines it is dug out of them and purified.

94420.q: Why must you never climb an electricity pylon?
a: There is a danger of death from electricity
Because it is too cold up there
94420.e: Power lines with a very high voltage hang from pylons. Even near them, you can get a deadly electric shock.

94421.q: How many volts does the overhead line above the SBB railway tracks carry?
94421.e: The SBB overhead line carries 15,000 volts. That is much more than in a socket and deadly dangerous.
94421.m: The SBB overhead line has 15,000 volts.

94422.q: Why must you never climb onto a railway carriage?
a: Electricity from the overhead line can jump across
The carriage has just been painted
94422.e: Electricity from the overhead line can jump through the air to a person. So you don't have to touch anything at all to get hurt.
94422.m: Climbing onto railway carriages is deadly dangerous.

94423.q: What do you do first if someone is still touching a device with electricity?
94423.e: Anyone who touches the person will get an electric shock too. So first pull out the plug or switch off the fuse, and get help.
94423.m: In an electrical accident, first switch off the electricity.

94424.q: Which emergency number do you call in Switzerland for an ambulance?
94424.e: The number 144 calls the ambulance service. 117 is the police and 118 the fire brigade. On 147, children and young people can talk about their worries.
94424.m: In Switzerland, you reach an ambulance on 144.

94425.q: What must you never put into a socket?
94425.e: Metal conducts electricity. Anyone who puts scissors or a nail into a socket gets a dangerous electric shock.
94425.m: Only a plug belongs in a socket.

94426.q: What does a yellow warning sign with a black lightning arrow mean?
94426.e: The yellow triangle with the lightning arrow warns of electrical voltage. You find it on electricity boxes and pylons.
94426.m: The lightning sign warns of electricity.

94427.q: Why doesn't a bird sitting on a power line get an electric shock?
94427.e: The bird sits on only one wire and touches nothing else. So no current flows through its body.
94427.m: A bird on just one wire stays safe.

94429.q: Why do you unplug a charger from the socket after charging?
a: It saves electricity and is safer
So that it charges faster next time
So that the cable doesn't rust
So that the socket stays clean
94429.e: A charger that is plugged in uses a little electricity even without a phone. Unplugging it saves energy and lowers the risk of fire.

94430.q: What do you need if a plug from another country doesn't fit into a Swiss socket?
94430.e: Many countries have different sockets. A travel adapter safely connects the foreign plug to the Swiss socket.
94430.m: For foreign plugs you need an adapter.

94431.q: Who should repair a broken socket in the flat?
94431.e: Working on electric wiring is dangerous and needs expert knowledge. That is why a trained professional does it.

94432.q: What do you do if a socket gives off sparks or looks broken?
a: Don't use it and tell an adult
94432.e: A broken socket can cause an electric shock or a fire. You don't use it and tell an adult straight away.

94433.q: What does a socket in the garden often have so that no rain gets in?
94433.e: Outdoor sockets have a lid that closes by itself. That way the inside stays dry.
94433.m: Outdoor sockets have a protective lid.

94434.q: How can you often tell that a plug in the socket has become too hot?
94434.e: If a plug gets too hot, plastic melts and there is a burning smell. Then an adult should switch off the electricity.
94434.m: A burning smell at a socket is a warning sign.

94435.q: Why does a multi-socket extension often have its own switch?
a: To switch off all devices at once
94435.e: With the switch on the extension, you disconnect all the devices plugged into it at the same time. That saves electricity used on standby.
94435.m: With the switch on the extension you switch everything off.

94934.q: What colour are the ripe berries of deadly nightshade?
94934.e: The ripe berries of deadly nightshade are black and shiny. They look like small cherries but are very poisonous.
94934.m: Never eat black, shiny berries in the forest.

94935.q: Why is deadly nightshade especially dangerous for children?
94935.e: The berries look like sweet cherries and even taste a little sweet. Just a few berries can seriously poison a child.
94935.m: What looks tasty is not always edible.

94936.q: Where does deadly nightshade often grow?
a: In the middle of a lake
94936.e: Deadly nightshade likes to grow in bright spots in the forest, for example in clearings and along forest paths.
94936.m: Deadly nightshade can grow in forest clearings.

94937.q: What does the fruit of deadly nightshade look like?
94937.e: The fruit is a round berry the size of a cherry. That is why its German name means “mad cherry”.
94937.m: Deadly nightshade has berries that look like cherries.

94938.q: What happens to the eyes when someone has eaten deadly nightshade?
94938.e: The poison of deadly nightshade makes the pupils, the black dots in the eye, very wide. Everything then looks blurred.
94938.m: Huge pupils can be a sign of deadly nightshade poisoning.

94939.q: Which parts of deadly nightshade are poisonous?
94939.e: With deadly nightshade, all parts are poisonous, including the leaves, root and berries.
94939.m: No part of deadly nightshade is safe.

94940.q: What colour are the flowers of deadly nightshade?
94940.e: The bell-shaped flowers of deadly nightshade are brownish to purple. They hang singly on the plant.
94940.m: Deadly nightshade has brownish purple bell flowers.

94941.q: How tall can deadly nightshade grow?
a: Up to about as tall as a person
94941.e: Deadly nightshade is a large perennial plant. It usually grows 50 to 150 centimetres tall, sometimes even 2 metres.
94941.m: Deadly nightshade is a large plant.

94942.q: What colour are the flowers of monkshood?
94942.e: Monkshood has dark blue to purple flowers.

94943.q: What does the shape of the monkshood flower remind you of?
94943.e: The top petal arches over the flower like a helmet or a hood.
94943.m: The monkshood flower looks like a knight's helmet.

94944.e: Monkshood is thought to be the most poisonous plant in Europe. Even small amounts can be life-threatening.
94944.m: Always leave monkshood where it is.

94945.q: Why should you not even pick monkshood with bare hands?
a: The poison goes through the skin
94945.e: The poison of monkshood can work through the skin and make it burn and tingle. That is why you should not touch it.

94946.q: Where does monkshood often grow in Switzerland?
94946.e: Monkshood likes to grow in damp meadows and near alpine huts in the mountains. But you can also find it in gardens.
94946.m: When hiking in the mountains you may see monkshood.

94947.q: Which animals like to visit monkshood flowers?
94947.e: Bumblebees are strong enough to crawl into the helmet-shaped flower to get nectar. While doing so, they pollinate the flower.

94948.q: What should you do if a friend wants to pick monkshood flowers?
a: Warn them and fetch an adult
Pick some too and smell them
Put the flowers in your mouth
94948.e: Monkshood is very poisonous. You warn your friend and tell an adult.
94948.m: With poisonous plants, warn others and get help.

94949.q: Roughly how tall does monkshood grow?
a: Only as tall as a finger
Only as tall as a shoe
94949.e: Monkshood usually grows 50 to 150 centimetres tall. It often reaches a child's hip or higher.

94951.q: What colour are the flowers of the common foxglove usually?
94951.e: The flowers are usually purple-red to pink. Inside they have dark spots with a pale edge.
94951.m: The common foxglove has purple-red flowers.

94952.q: How are the flowers arranged on the stem of the foxglove?
a: One below the other on one side
As a single flower at the top
94952.e: Lots of flowers hang one below the other on one side of the tall stem, like bells on a pole.
94952.m: On the foxglove, lots of flowers hang on a long stem.

94953.q: Which organ does foxglove poison especially affect?
94953.e: Foxglove poison affects the heart. That is why all parts of the plant are dangerous.
94953.m: Foxglove is a poison for the heart.

94954.q: What are substances from the foxglove used for in medicine?
94954.e: Doctors use carefully measured active substances from the foxglove to strengthen weak hearts. You must never take the plant yourself.
94954.m: Only doctors may give foxglove substances as medicine.

94955.q: Which insect likes to crawl into foxglove flowers?
94955.e: Bumblebees crawl right into the big flower tubes. The spots inside show them the way to the nectar.
94955.m: The spots inside the foxglove show the bumblebee the way.

94956.q: Where does the common foxglove often grow?
a: At the edge of the forest
94956.e: The common foxglove likes to grow at forest edges and in forest clearings. Many people also plant it in their gardens.
94956.m: Foxgloves can glow at the edge of the forest.

94957.q: Which parts of the common foxglove are poisonous?
94957.e: With the foxglove, the leaves, flowers, stem and seeds are poisonous.
94957.m: Every part of the foxglove is poisonous.

94958.q: In which month does lily of the valley usually flower?
94958.e: Lily of the valley mainly flowers in May. Its German name even means “little May bell”.
94958.m: Lily of the valley flowers in May.

94959.q: What colour are the berries of lily of the valley?
94959.e: After flowering, lily of the valley forms small red berries. They are poisonous too.
94959.m: The red berries of lily of the valley are poisonous.

94960.q: What do lily of the valley flowers smell like?
94960.e: Lily of the valley has a strong, sweet scent. That is why some people put it in a vase.
94960.m: Lily of the valley smells sweet but is poisonous.

94961.q: What should you do after picking lily of the valley?
94961.e: Some of the poison can stick to your hands. That is why you wash them well after touching it.
94961.m: Wash your hands after touching poisonous plants.

94962.q: Why should you not drink the water from a vase of lily of the valley?
94962.e: The poison of lily of the valley can get into the vase water. That is why the water should be poured away.
94962.m: Vase water from lily of the valley is not for drinking.

94963.q: In which season does the autumn crocus flower?
94963.e: The autumn crocus flowers in September and October, so in autumn. That is where its name comes from.
94963.m: The autumn crocus flowers in autumn.

94964.q: What colour are the flowers of the autumn crocus?
94964.e: The flowers are delicate lilac to pale purple and stand straight up out of the meadow.
94964.m: The autumn crocus has pale purple flowers.

94965.q: Which spring flower does the flower of the autumn crocus look like?
94965.e: The flower looks like a crocus. But the crocus flowers in spring.
94965.m: A lilac crocus in autumn is often an autumn crocus.

94966.q: What is special about the flower of the autumn crocus?
a: It only flowers once in ten years
94966.e: In autumn you only see the flower. The leaves only grow the following spring.
94966.m: In autumn the autumn crocus shows only its flower.

94967.q: When do the leaves of the autumn crocus grow?
94967.e: The leaves appear in spring together with the seed capsule, but without a flower. Then they can be mistaken for edible wild herbs.
94967.m: The leaves of the autumn crocus come in spring.

94968.q: Where does the autumn crocus often grow?
94968.e: The autumn crocus likes to grow in damp meadows and pastures, in Switzerland too.
94968.m: The autumn crocus can grow in autumn meadows.

94969.q: Why do farmers not let their cows eat the autumn crocus?
94969.e: The autumn crocus is very poisonous, for people and for cows, horses and sheep. That is why farmers watch out for it.
94969.m: The autumn crocus is poisonous for grazing animals too.

94970.q: What does the autumn crocus grow back from every year?
a: From a corm in the ground
94970.e: The autumn crocus has a corm in the ground. New flowers and leaves grow from it every year.
94970.m: The autumn crocus survives the winter as a corm.

94971.e: Mezereon flowers from February or March, often while there is still snow on the ground.
94971.m: Mezereon is one of the first plants to flower each year.

94972.q: What colour are the flowers of mezereon usually?
94972.e: The small flowers are pink to purple-red. Occasionally there are white ones too.

94973.q: Where are the flowers on mezereon?
a: At the top of long stalks
94973.e: The flowers sit closely together directly on the bare twigs. The leaves only grow after flowering.
94973.m: On mezereon, the bare twigs flower.

94974.q: What kind of plant is mezereon?
94974.e: Mezereon is a small shrub, usually only about a metre tall.

94975.q: What colour are the berries of mezereon?
94975.e: In late summer mezereon has bright red berries. They are very poisonous.
94975.m: The red berries of mezereon are poisonous.

94976.q: What do mezereon flowers smell like?
94976.e: The flowers have a strong, sweet scent. This attracts insects in early spring.
94976.m: Mezereon smells strongly, but you do not pick it.

94977.q: What happens if mezereon sap gets on your skin?
a: Your skin can go red and burn
Your skin goes as hard as wood
94977.e: The bark and sap contain a harsh poison. On the skin it can cause redness and blisters.

94978.q: Where does mezereon grow in the wild?
94978.e: Mezereon grows in deciduous forests and mountain forests, in Switzerland too.
94978.m: You can discover mezereon in the forest.

94979.e: The flowers are bright yellow like gold. That is why laburnum is also called golden rain.

94980.q: How do laburnum flowers hang on the tree?
a: One by one on the ground
Not at all, it never flowers
94980.e: The flowers hang down in long clusters. It looks like golden rain.
94980.m: Laburnum looks like falling golden rain.

94981.q: Where do you find laburnum especially often?
94981.e: Laburnum is a popular ornamental tree. That is why it is often found in gardens and parks.
94981.m: Poisonous plants can grow in gardens too.

94982.q: What do the fruits of laburnum look like?
94982.e: After flowering, laburnum forms pods similar to beans or peas. The seeds are inside.

94983.q: Why are laburnum pods dangerous for children?
a: They look like beans to play with
94983.e: Children like to play at cooking with the bean-like pods and seeds. But the seeds are especially poisonous.
94983.m: Do not play at cooking with laburnum pods.

94984.q: Which parts of laburnum are poisonous?
94984.e: All parts of laburnum are poisonous, the seeds most of all.

94985.q: What kind of plant is laburnum?
94985.e: Laburnum is a small tree or large shrub and grows several metres tall.
94985.m: Laburnum is a tree with yellow flowers.

94986.q: In which season does laburnum flower?
94986.e: Laburnum flowers in spring, from about April to June.
94986.m: In May, yellow flowers hang from the laburnum.

94987.q: What colour are the ripe berries of lords-and-ladies?
94987.e: In summer, lots of bright red berries sit close together on a spike. They are poisonous.
94987.m: Leave red berries on a spike in the forest alone.

94988.q: How are the berries of lords-and-ladies arranged?
94988.e: The berries sit close together on an upright spike. It looks like a small corn cob.
94988.m: Lords-and-ladies has its berries on a spike.

94989.q: What wraps around the flower of lords-and-ladies?
94989.e: The flower sits inside a large, greenish leaf wrapped around it like a paper cone.
94989.m: The flower of lords-and-ladies sits in a cone-shaped leaf.

94990.q: How does lords-and-ladies hold small insects in its flower for a short time?
a: In a trap made of hairs
94990.e: Small midges slide into the chamber at the bottom of the flower. Hairs hold them there until the next morning. By then they are covered in pollen and are allowed out again.
94990.m: Lords-and-ladies traps insects for a short time so they pollinate it.

94991.e: Lords-and-ladies likes damp, shady deciduous forests.

94992.q: Which edible plant can young lords-and-ladies leaves be mistaken for?
94992.e: Young lords-and-ladies leaves often grow among wild garlic. That is why you must check every leaf carefully when picking.
94992.m: Watch out for lords-and-ladies when picking wild garlic.

94993.q: What shape are the leaves of lords-and-ladies?
94993.e: The leaves are large and arrow-shaped, often with dark spots. That is why it is also called spotted arum.

94994.q: What happens if you bite into a piece of lords-and-ladies?
94994.e: The plant contains harsh substances. They burn in your mouth and throat.
94994.m: Lords-and-ladies burns in your mouth and is poisonous.

94995.q: How can you recognise hemlock by its stem?
94995.e: The stem has reddish-brown to purple spots. That is why it is called spotted hemlock.
94995.m: Red spots on the stem warn you of hemlock.

94996.q: What does hemlock smell of when you crush it?
94996.e: Crushed leaves have a nasty smell of mouse wee. But it is better not to crush it at all.

94997.e: Hemlock has lots of small white flowers in clusters that look like umbrellas.
94997.m: Hemlock has small white umbrella-shaped flower clusters.

94998.q: What do the flower clusters of hemlock look like?
94998.e: The flowers form umbels. They look like open umbrellas.
94998.m: Many poisonous meadow plants have flowers like umbrellas.

94999.q: Which kitchen herb can young hemlock leaves be mistaken for?
94999.e: The finely feathered leaves of hemlock look similar to parsley.
94999.m: Only pick wild herbs with an expert.

95000.e: Hemlock is one of the most poisonous plants here. Even a little of it is dangerous.

95001.e: You find it along paths, hedges, waste ground and riverbanks.
95001.m: Poisonous plants can grow along paths too.

a: Only as tall as a fingernail
95002.e: Hemlock often grows 1 to 2 metres tall, sometimes even taller.

95003.q: What happens if the sap of giant hogweed gets on your skin and then the sun shines?
a: Your skin turns yellow and never itches
95003.e: The sap makes the skin sensitive to sunlight. Then painful blisters appear, like burns.
95003.m: Giant hogweed and sun together burn the skin.

95004.q: How tall can giant hogweed grow?
95004.e: Giant hogweed grows up to about 3 metres tall, so much taller than an adult.
95004.m: Giant hogweed is taller than a person.

95005.q: What colour are the flowers of giant hogweed?
95005.e: Giant hogweed has white flowers in huge umbrella-shaped clusters.

95006.q: How big can the flower umbrellas of giant hogweed get?
a: As big as a bike wheel
95006.e: The flower umbrellas are often 30 to 50 centimetres wide. That is about as big as a small bike wheel.
95006.m: The flower umbrellas of giant hogweed are huge.

95007.q: Where does giant hogweed often grow here?
a: In the middle of a deep lake
95007.e: Giant hogweed likes damp places, by streams, forest edges and paths. You need to watch out for it there.
95007.m: Giant hogweed often grows by streams and paths.

95008.q: What should you do if sap from giant hogweed has got on your skin?
a: Wash it and keep out of the sun
95008.e: Wash the spot well with water straight away and protect it from the sun. Then tell an adult.
95008.m: After touching hogweed, wash your skin and keep out of the sun.

95009.q: Why should you not make blowpipes out of giant hogweed stems?
a: The sap burns the skin in sunlight
The stems are made of glass
95009.e: The hollow stems are tempting for making things. But sap on your mouth can cause bad burns in the sun.
95009.m: Never make things or play with giant hogweed.

95010.e: Giant hogweed flowers in summer, around June and July.
95010.m: In summer you see the giant white umbrellas.

95011.q: What do you often see on your skin after touching a stinging nettle?
95011.e: Small white or red bumps appear on the skin. They sting and itch for a while.

95012.q: Does the sting of a nettle usually go away again?
95012.e: The stinging is unpleasant, but usually goes away by itself after a few hours.
95012.m: Nettle stings hurt, but they pass.

95013.q: Which animals like to eat nettle leaves?
95013.e: The caterpillars of the peacock butterfly and the small tortoiseshell eat nettle leaves.
95013.m: Without nettles, some caterpillars would have no food.

95014.q: What can you make from nettle leaves?
95014.e: Dried or cooked nettle leaves no longer sting. You can make tea or soup from them.
95014.m: Dried or cooked nettles no longer sting.

95015.q: Where do stinging nettles often grow?
95015.e: Nettles like to grow on nutrient-rich soil, for example along paths, fences and streams.
95015.m: Nettles like to grow along paths.

95016.q: What is the best way to protect yourself from stinging nettles?
95016.e: Long trousers and sleeves protect your skin from the stinging hairs.
95016.m: Long trousers protect you from nettles.

95017.q: What helps when your skin stings after touching nettles?
95017.e: Rinsing the spot with cool water calms the skin. Scratching usually makes it worse.

95018.q: When can you call the poisons helpline 145?
95018.e: Tox Info Suisse can be reached day and night, on every day of the year.
95018.m: You can always reach the poisons helpline 145.

95019.q: Which number do you dial if a poisoned child is unconscious?
95019.e: If someone is unconscious, the ambulance service is needed immediately. You call it on 144.
95019.m: If someone is unconscious, call the ambulance on 144.

95020.q: Should you make someone sick after they have eaten a poisonous plant?
95020.e: Tox Info Suisse advises not to make someone vomit. It is better to call 145 straight away.
95020.m: In a poisoning, do not make someone vomit.

95021.q: What do you take to the doctor if someone has eaten part of a plant?
95021.e: A piece of the plant or a photo helps the experts identify the plant.
95021.m: A piece of the plant helps to identify it.

95022.q: In which city is Tox Info Suisse based?
95022.e: Tox Info Suisse, the Swiss poisons information centre, is based in Zurich.
95022.m: The Swiss poisons information centre is in Zurich.

95023.q: What is the first thing you do if a little brother or sister has eaten a poisonous berry?
95023.e: Tell an adult straight away. They will then call 145.
95023.m: In a poisoning, fetch an adult straight away.

95024.q: What is the rule for unknown berries in the forest?
a: Never eat them without an adult
95024.e: Many poisonous berries look tasty. Only eat berries that an adult knows for sure.

95025.q: What should you do if plant sap has got into your eye?
95025.e: Tox Info Suisse advises rinsing the eye with lukewarm water for 10 to 15 minutes while keeping it open.
95025.m: Rinse anything that splashed into your eye with water for a long time.

95026.q: How do the flowers of lily of the valley hang on the stalk?
a: As a single flower at the top
95026.e: On lily of the valley, 5 to 10 little bell flowers hang in a row, all on the same side.
95026.m: The little bells of lily of the valley hang in a row.

95027.q: How many large leaves does lily of the valley usually have?
95027.e: Lily of the valley usually has two, occasionally three, broad leaves. The flower stalk grows between them.
95027.m: Lily of the valley usually has two leaves.

95028.q: Where does lily of the valley grow in the wild?
95028.e: Lily of the valley grows wild in bright deciduous forests, where it often forms large carpets.
95028.m: You can see carpets of lily of the valley in deciduous forests.

95029.q: Which plant looks similar to the stinging nettle but does not sting?
95029.e: The dead-nettle has similar leaves but no stinging hairs. It is called “dead” because it does not sting.

95030.q: What will the expert on the poisons helpline want to know from you?
a: What was eaten, how much and when
95030.e: So that the experts can help, they need to know exactly what someone ate, how much and when. The person's age is important too.
95030.m: On the poisons helpline, say what was eaten, how much and when.

95031.q: The scientific name of deadly nightshade contains the word “belladonna”. What does that mean in Italian?
95031.e: “Bella donna” means beautiful woman in Italian. In the past, women used the plant for beauty, which was very dangerous.

95032.q: How long does a common foxglove plant usually live?
95032.e: In the first year, only a clump of leaves grows on the ground. The foxglove only flowers in its second year, and then it usually dies.
95032.m: The foxglove only flowers in its second year.

95033.q: Which parts of monkshood are poisonous?
95033.e: With monkshood, all parts are poisonous. The most poison is in the root tuber.

95092.q: In which year was penicillin discovered?
95092.e: In 1928 Alexander Fleming noticed that a mould was killing bacteria in his dish. Later it was turned into a medicine.

95093.q: Which living thing was the first penicillin obtained from?
95093.e: Penicillin is made by a green mould. The mould uses it to fight off bacteria.

95094.q: Who prescribes an antibiotic in Switzerland?
95094.e: In Switzerland, antibiotics you swallow are only available on prescription. The doctor decides whether you need one.
95094.m: An antibiotic is prescribed by a doctor.

95095.q: How long should you take an antibiotic for?
a: As long as the doctor says
95095.e: You take an antibiotic exactly as it was prescribed. Otherwise some bacteria may survive.
95095.m: You take an antibiotic exactly as instructed.

95096.q: What can happen if antibiotics are used too often?
95096.e: Some bacteria get used to antibiotics. Then the medicines no longer work well. This is called resistance.
95096.m: Too many antibiotics make bacteria resistant.

95097.q: Where do you collect an antibiotic with a prescription?
95097.e: You get medicines at the chemist's. For an antibiotic, you show the doctor's prescription there.
95097.m: Prescription medicines are collected at the chemist's.

95098.q: Besides water, what do you need to wash germs off your hands properly?
95098.e: Soap loosens grease and dirt from the skin. The germs are then rinsed away with the water.
95098.m: Soap gets your hands really clean.

95099.q: When should you definitely wash your hands?
a: After getting up from a chair
95099.e: Lots of germs get onto your hands in the toilet. Washing your hands stops them being passed on.
95099.m: Always wash your hands after using the toilet.

95100.q: Why do doctors disinfect their hands before treating someone?
a: So they don't pass on germs that cause illness
95100.e: Bacteria and viruses can travel from one person to the next on hands. Disinfecting kills most germs.
95100.m: Clean hands stop illnesses being passed on.

a: Tiny living things that can make you ill
95101.e: Germs are so small that you can only see them under a microscope. Some of them can make you ill.
95101.m: Germs are tiny and can make you ill.

95102.q: What is the best thing to dry your hands with after washing them?
95102.e: A clean towel has few germs on it. Clothes and hair, on the other hand, can put dirt back on your hands.
95102.m: Dry your hands on a clean towel after washing.

95103.q: Which parts are easy to forget when washing your hands?
95103.e: People often don't wash enough between their fingers and around their thumbs. That is why you should rub your fingers together.
95103.m: When washing your hands, rub between your fingers too.

95104.q: What can you use for clean hands when you are out and there is no water?
95104.e: Hand sanitiser kills many germs without water. You rub it in until your hands are dry.

95105.q: Which number do you dial in Switzerland for an ambulance?
95105.e: In Switzerland, 144 connects you to the ambulance service. 117 is the police and 118 is the fire brigade.
95105.m: The ambulance number in Switzerland is 144.

95106.q: What is the number of Rega, the Swiss air rescue service?
95106.e: You can reach Rega on 1414. It helps with helicopters, for example in the mountains.

95107.q: Which emergency number works all over Europe, including Switzerland?
95107.e: 112 is the European emergency number. It also works in Switzerland, even from a mobile phone.
95107.m: 112 is the emergency number all over Europe.

95108.q: What do you do first for a small burn on your hand?
95108.e: Cool running water eases the pain of small burns. Butter or flour should never go on a burn.
95108.m: Cool a small burn with water.

95109.q: How do you position an unconscious person who is breathing normally?
95109.e: In the recovery position the airway stays clear. Vomit can run out of the mouth instead of getting into the lungs.
95109.m: Put an unconscious person who is breathing in the recovery position.

95110.q: How do you hold your head when you have a nosebleed?
95110.e: With your head forward, the blood runs out of your nose and not down your throat. A cool cloth on the back of the neck can help.
95110.m: With a nosebleed, tilt your head forward.

95111.q: At an accident, what do you check first before you help?
95111.e: Anyone who helps should not put themselves in danger. First look around, then think and then act.
95111.m: When helping, check your own safety first.

95112.q: Which number do you call in Switzerland if someone has swallowed something poisonous?
95112.e: On 145 you reach Tox Info Suisse. Experts there help with poisoning, day and night.

95113.q: Which flag looks like the Red Cross flag with the colours swapped?
95113.e: The Red Cross has a red cross on a white background. It was chosen in honour of Switzerland, whose flag has the colours the other way round.
95113.m: The Red Cross emblem is the Swiss flag reversed.

95114.q: In which Swiss city does the International Committee of the Red Cross have its headquarters?
95114.e: The International Committee of the Red Cross, ICRC for short, has its headquarters in Geneva. From there it helps in many countries.
95114.m: The ICRC has its headquarters in Geneva.

95115.q: Which emblem does the Red Cross movement use in many Muslim countries?
95115.e: Besides the Red Cross there is the Red Crescent. Both belong to the same aid movement.
95115.m: In many countries the aid movement is called the Red Crescent.

95116.q: Who does the Red Cross help especially in wars?
95116.e: The Red Cross helps everyone in need, no matter which side they are on. It also visits prisoners of war.
95116.m: The Red Cross helps the wounded and prisoners.

95117.q: What do many adults donate through the Swiss Red Cross to help sick people?
95117.e: Blood donations are important for operations and accidents. In Switzerland the Red Cross blood donation service organises the donations.
95117.m: Giving blood can help sick people.

95118.q: What is the abbreviation for the Swiss Red Cross?
95118.e: SRK stands for Schweizerisches Rotes Kreuz, the Swiss Red Cross. It helps in Switzerland, for example with transport services and courses.
95118.m: The Swiss Red Cross is called SRK for short.

95119.q: What does the Red Cross emblem on a vehicle mean in a war?
95119.e: The Red Cross emblem is a protective sign. Anyone using it to help the wounded must not be attacked in a war.
95119.m: The Red Cross emblem protects helpers in war.

95120.q: At which battle in Italy did Henry Dunant see thousands of wounded in 1859?
95120.e: After the Battle of Solferino, many wounded lay there with no help. Dunant helped care for them together with women from the village.
95120.m: Henry Dunant witnessed the Battle of Solferino in 1859.

95121.q: Which prize did Henry Dunant receive in 1901 as one of the first winners?
95121.e: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded for the first time in 1901. Henry Dunant shared it with the Frenchman Frédéric Passy.
95121.m: Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

95122.q: What did Henry Dunant write after the war of 1859 to shake people up?
95122.e: In his book Dunant described the suffering of the wounded. He suggested setting up aid groups in every country.
95122.m: Henry Dunant wrote a book about the suffering in war.

95123.q: Which aid organisation did Henry Dunant help to found?
95123.e: In 1863 Dunant and others founded the committee in Geneva that became the International Red Cross.
95123.m: Henry Dunant helped to found the Red Cross.

95124.q: What was Henry Dunant's original job?
95124.e: Dunant was a merchant and travelled to see Emperor Napoleon III about a business deal. That is how he came to the battlefield.
95124.m: Henry Dunant was originally a businessman.

95125.q: Which aid organisation was founded by the Swiss Henry Dunant?
95125.e: Henry Dunant saw many wounded soldiers after a battle. So he founded the Red Cross, which helps the injured.
95125.m: Henry Dunant founded the Red Cross.

95126.q: Which sense tells you whether something is rough or smooth?
95126.e: With the sense of touch you feel what a surface is like. You need neither eyes nor ears for it.
95126.m: With the sense of touch you feel rough and smooth.

95127.q: Where on the hand are there especially many touch receptors?
a: On the back of the hand
95127.e: There are a great many tiny sensors in the fingertips. That is why you can feel things especially finely with them.

95128.q: What do ants use to feel their way?
95128.e: Ants touch the ground and other ants with their movable antennae. They can also smell with them.

95129.q: Which part of its body does an elephant use to feel things especially finely?
95129.e: The tip of an elephant's trunk is very sensitive. With it, the elephant can even feel and grab small things like a peanut.
95129.m: An elephant feels things with its trunk.

95130.q: What do you say about someone who does a difficult thing very carefully and skilfully?
95130.e: Having a delicate touch means being sensitive and skilful. The phrase comes from the fine sense of touch in the fingers.
95130.m: Someone who is skilful and sensitive has a delicate touch.

95131.q: Where do the nerves report what the fingers feel?
95131.e: The nerves carry the messages from the skin to the brain in a flash. Only there do you notice what you are touching.
95131.m: The brain processes what the skin feels.

95132.q: What do babies very often use to feel objects?
95132.e: Lips and tongue can feel very finely. That is why babies put lots of things in their mouth to explore them.
95132.m: Babies often explore things with their mouth.

95133.q: What can you find out by touch with your eyes closed?
a: Whether something is soft or hard
95133.e: When you touch something, you feel whether it gives way or is firm. Colours and brightness, on the other hand, can only be seen.
95133.m: By touch you feel whether something is soft or hard.

95134.q: What do cats use to feel their surroundings in the dark?
95134.e: A cat's whiskers are very sensitive. They can feel even tiny movements of air and narrow gaps.

95135.q: What does a glowing sign on a switched-off hob mean?
95135.e: Even after it is switched off, a hob stays hot for a long time. The display warns you not to touch it.
95135.m: A heat warning light warns of a hot hob.

95136.q: What do you call a lightning-fast movement of the body that happens without thinking?
95136.e: In a reflex, the body reacts by itself and very quickly. This protects us from injuries.
95136.m: A reflex is a movement without thinking.

95137.q: What do you use to hold a hot pan?
95137.e: A thick oven glove only lets the heat through slowly. That way you do not burn your hands.
95137.m: You hold hot pans with an oven glove.

95138.q: What does the body do in great heat to cool down?
95138.e: Sweat comes out of the skin and evaporates. This makes the skin cooler.
95138.m: In the heat, the body cools down by sweating.

95139.q: Which part of the body do parents often use to check that a baby's bath water is not too hot?
95139.e: The skin on the elbow is thinner and less used to heat than the palm of the hand. So you can easily tell whether the water feels pleasant.
95139.m: You check the warmth of bath water with your elbow.

95140.q: What does your skin get if you stay in the sun too long without protection?
95140.e: The sun's rays damage the skin. It turns red, hot and painful. Sun cream and shade protect you.
95140.m: Too much sun gives you sunburn.

95141.q: What can form on the skin when you burn yourself?
95141.e: With a burn, fluid collects under the skin. This forms a blister, which you should not burst.
95141.m: A burn can cause a blister.

95142.q: Why should you not walk barefoot over hot tarmac in summer?
a: You can burn the soles of your feet
It makes you tired straight away
95142.e: Dark tarmac gets very hot in the sun. The skin on the soles of your feet can get burnt.
95142.m: Hot tarmac can burn the soles of your feet.

95143.q: What do you get on your skin when you are cold?
95143.e: In the cold, the tiny hairs stand up and the skin forms little bumps. In Switzerland people call this “chicken skin”.
95143.m: When you are cold, you get goose bumps.

95144.q: What does the body do to make heat when it is very cold?
95144.e: When you shiver, your muscles move very fast. This makes heat.
95144.m: Shivering warms the body in the cold.

95145.q: Which parts of the body usually get cold first?
95145.e: In the cold, the body sends warm blood mainly to the important organs. That is why fingers and toes get cold quickly.
95145.m: Fingers and toes get cold first.

95146.q: What is an injury to the skin caused by extreme cold called?
95146.e: In extreme cold, the skin on fingers, toes, ears or nose can be damaged. This is called frostbite.

95147.q: What protects your hands from the cold in winter?
95147.e: Gloves hold the warm air around your hands. That way your fingers do not cool down so quickly.
95147.m: Gloves keep your hands warm in winter.

95148.q: What happens to your hand if you hold an ice cube for a long time?
95148.e: The cold slows down the nerves in the skin. Then you feel almost nothing and your hand goes numb.
95148.m: Great cold makes the skin numb.

95149.q: What do you put on a fresh bump on the head?
95149.e: Cold makes the swelling less bad and eases the pain. Never put ice directly on the skin.

95150.q: Why does a metal railing feel colder in winter than a wooden one?
a: Wood is always in the sun
95150.e: Metal takes the warmth from your hand very quickly. That is why it feels colder, even when it is just as cold as the wood.
95150.m: Metal feels cold because it carries heat away quickly.

95151.q: Why is pain useful for the body?
95151.e: Pain is a warning signal. It shows that something is hurting the body or that something is wrong.

95152.q: What is a medicine that eases pain called?
95152.e: A painkiller dulls the pain. Children should only take it when an adult allows it.

95153.q: What does the number 0 mean on a pain scale from 0 to 10?
95153.e: With the pain scale you show the doctor how much something hurts. 0 means no pain, 10 the worst.
95153.m: On the pain scale, 0 means no pain.

95154.q: What is a blue mark that appears after a knock called?
95154.e: When you knock yourself, tiny blood vessels under the skin burst. The blood collects there and shows through blue.
95154.m: A blue mark is a bruise.

95155.q: What do you feel when you knock your funny bone on your elbow?
a: A warm tickle in your tummy
95155.e: At the elbow, a nerve lies right under the skin. If you hit it, it tingles all the way to your fingers.
95155.m: At the funny bone, a nerve lies right under the skin.

95157.q: What usually happens to the skin after a wasp sting?
95157.e: When a wasp stings, it injects a little poison into the skin. The spot turns red, swells and hurts.
95157.m: A wasp sting swells up and hurts.

95158.q: What should you do if a pain does not go away for a long time?
95158.e: Long or strong pain can be a sign of an illness. A doctor can find out where it comes from.
95158.m: With long-lasting pain you go to the doctor.

95159.q: Why can you not really tickle yourself?
a: The brain knows in advance where it will be touched
Your own fingers are too cold
95159.e: The brain plans your own movement and expects the touch. So the surprise is gone and it does not tickle.

95160.q: Where are many people especially ticklish?
a: On the soles of the feet
On the top of the head
95160.e: There are many sensitive nerves on the soles of the feet. A light touch there tickles many people a lot.
95160.m: Many people are ticklish on the soles of their feet.

95161.q: What do most people do when they are tickled?
95161.e: Tickling makes most people laugh. That happens even though it is not always pleasant.
95161.m: Most people laugh when they are tickled.

95162.q: Which animals make a laughing sound when tickled?
95162.e: Young chimpanzees and other great apes also pant when tickled, as if they were laughing. This is how they play together.

95163.q: What often makes you sneeze when your nose tickles?
95163.e: Dust irritates the lining of the nose. By sneezing, the body blasts it back out.
95163.m: Dust in the nose makes you sneeze.

95164.q: What should you do if someone says “Stop” while you are tickling them?
95164.e: Tickling can become unpleasant. Anyone who says stop must be taken seriously.
95164.m: If someone says stop, you stop.

95165.q: What do you feel when an ant crawls over your arm?
95165.e: Its little legs touch the fine hairs on the skin. You feel this as a light tingling or tickling.
95165.m: A crawling ant tingles on the skin.

95166.e: Blind people and people with very poor sight can read Braille. They do not need their eyes for it.

95167.q: What can you use to write Braille?
95167.e: A Braille writing machine presses the dots into thick paper from below. Today there are also printers for it.
95167.m: Braille is written with a Braille writing machine.

95168.q: How did Louis Braille become blind as a small child?
a: Through an accident in the workshop
Through a fall from a horse
95168.e: At about three years old, he hurt his eye with a sharp tool in his father's workshop. Later he went blind in both eyes.
95168.m: Louis Braille went blind through an accident.

95169.q: Where did Louis Braille hurt his eye as a small child?
95169.e: At about three years old, he was playing with a sharp tool in his father's workshop. He hurt his eye and later went completely blind.
95169.m: Louis Braille hurt himself in his father's workshop.

95170.q: Why are books in Braille much thicker than other books?
a: The dots take up a lot of space
The paper is made of wood
95170.e: The dots must be big enough to feel. That is why much less text fits on a page.
95170.m: Books in Braille are very thick.

95171.q: Roughly how old was Louis Braille when he invented his dot writing?
95171.e: Louis Braille finished his dot writing in 1825. He was only 16 years old at the time.
95171.m: Louis Braille was still a teenager when he invented the writing.

95172.q: Which writing for soldiers gave Louis Braille his idea?
a: A writing for reading in the dark
A writing made of smoke signals
95172.e: An army officer had invented a night writing made of raised dots. Braille turned it into a simpler writing.
95172.m: A night writing for soldiers gave Braille his idea.

95173.q: What do the signs of Braille feel like?
95173.e: The dots are pressed out of the paper. You feel them as little raised bumps.
95173.m: The dots of Braille stand out from the paper.

95174.q: What do you do on a barefoot trail?
95174.e: On a barefoot trail you take off your shoes and socks. With your bare feet you feel the ground.
95174.m: On a barefoot trail you walk without shoes.

95175.q: What do you feel with your feet on a barefoot trail?
95175.e: A barefoot trail goes over grass, sand, stones, bark or mud. Each surface feels different.
95175.m: On a barefoot trail you feel different surfaces.

95176.q: Which surface feels especially soft on a barefoot trail?
95176.e: Moss is a soft, damp cushion of tiny plants. Walking on it feels like walking on a carpet.
95176.m: Moss feels soft under your feet.

95177.q: Which surface prickles most under your feet?
95177.e: Fir cones are hard and spiky. Walking on them prickles the soles of your feet.
95177.m: Fir cones prickle under your feet.

95178.q: What should you do after a barefoot trail?
95178.e: After a barefoot trail your feet are often dirty. That is why many barefoot trails have a basin for washing at the end.
95178.m: After a barefoot trail you wash your feet.

95179.q: What gets especially strong when you walk barefoot?
95179.e: Without shoes, the small muscles in the foot work harder. That keeps the feet strong and flexible.
95179.m: Walking barefoot strengthens the foot muscles.

95180.q: In which canton is the well-known barefoot trail from Jakobsbad to Gontenbad?
95180.e: The barefoot trail runs through the hilly countryside near Gonten in the Appenzell region. It is a few kilometres long.
95180.m: A well-known barefoot trail is in the Appenzell region.

95181.q: Why is the grass often wet early in the morning?
95181.e: In the cool night, tiny drops of water from the air form on the grass. This is the dew.
95181.m: In the morning the grass is wet with dew.

95182.q: In which season do people most like going on a barefoot trail?
95182.e: In summer the ground is warm and pleasant. In winter and cool times it would be too cold for bare feet.
95182.m: Barefoot trails are best in summer.

95183.q: What do you do with a feely box?
95183.e: You reach into the box through a hole. You have to guess what is inside only by touch.
95183.m: In a feely box you recognise things by touch.

95184.q: Which parts of the body do you use most with a feely box?
95184.e: The objects are hidden so you cannot see them. You only recognise them by grabbing and feeling them.
95184.m: With a feely box you recognise things with your hands.

95185.q: What does a fir cone feel like in the feely box?
95185.e: A fir cone has lots of hard, scale-like parts. You can feel the edges well with your fingers.
95185.m: A fir cone feels rough and scaly.

95186.q: Which object feels soft and fluffy?
95186.e: Cotton wool is made of many fine fibres with air in between. That is why it is soft and fluffy.
95186.m: Cotton wool feels soft and fluffy.

95187.q: Which object feels smooth and cool?
95187.e: A metal spoon has no grooves and no fibres. It feels smooth and cool.
95187.m: A metal spoon feels smooth and cool.

95188.q: How do you recognise a walnut in the feely box?
a: It is hard with a wrinkly shell
95188.e: The shell of a walnut is hard and has lots of grooves. You can feel that well with your fingers.
95188.m: A walnut has a hard, wrinkly shell.

95189.q: Which object is soft, has lots of holes and soaks up water?
95189.e: A sponge is full of tiny holes. You can squeeze it and it takes in water.
95189.m: A sponge is soft and full of holes.

95190.q: Why should nothing sharp go into a feely box?
a: So that the box is lighter
So that you can see more
95190.e: You reach into the box without looking. Pointed or sharp things could hurt your hands.
95190.m: Nothing sharp goes into a feely box.

95191.q: What do you do almost automatically when something itches?
95191.e: An itch makes you want to scratch. Scratching helps for a moment, but it can irritate the skin.
95191.m: When something itches, you want to scratch.

95192.q: What itches for many people in spring when pollen is in the air?
95192.e: With hay fever, the body reacts to pollen. Then your eyes and nose itch and you have to sneeze.
95192.m: With hay fever, pollen makes your eyes and nose itch.

95193.q: Which plant stings and itches on the skin when you touch it?
95193.e: The stinging nettle has fine stinging hairs. When you touch them, they break off and release a burning juice into the skin. Small red bumps then appear that itch.
95193.m: The stinging nettle stings and itches on the skin.

95194.q: What often itches when a graze is healing?
95194.e: New skin grows under the scab. This often itches, but you should not pick off the scab.

95195.q: What can happen if you scratch a mosquito bite until it bleeds?
95195.e: Scratching gets dirt and germs into the little wound. Then it can get infected.

95196.q: Which small creatures can make your head itch and turn up in school classes?
95196.e: Head lice live in the hair. Their bites itch, and they do not jump but crawl from head to head.
95196.m: Head lice make your head itch.

95197.q: Which childhood illness causes lots of itchy blisters all over the body?
95197.e: With chickenpox, lots of small, itchy blisters appear on the skin. In Switzerland it is also called “Wilde Blattern”.

95198.q: What helps against dry, itchy skin in winter?
95198.e: A good cream keeps the skin moist and soft. Then it itches less.
95198.m: Putting cream on helps against dry skin.

95199.q: What do you feel when a shoe is too small?
95199.e: If a shoe is too small, it presses on your toes and foot. You feel this as unpleasant pressure.
95199.m: A shoe that is too small pinches.

95200.q: How do you check with your thumb whether a bicycle tyre has enough air?
95200.e: A well-pumped tyre hardly gives when you press it. If it is soft, it needs more air.
95200.m: By pressing, you check whether a tyre has enough air.

95201.q: What do you feel in your ears when you dive deep in the swimming pool?
95201.e: The deeper you dive, the more water presses down from above. You feel this especially in your ears.
95201.m: When diving, you feel pressure in your ears.

95202.q: What does a sock top that is too tight leave on your skin?
95202.e: The elastic presses into the skin for a long time. Afterwards you see red lines that soon disappear.
95202.m: Tight socks leave marks on the skin.

95203.q: What does the doctor measure with an inflatable cuff on the upper arm?
95203.e: The cuff squeezes the arm for a moment. A device measures how strongly the blood presses against the blood vessels.
95203.m: The cuff is used to measure blood pressure.

95204.q: Why does a pointed stone under your foot hurt more than a flat one?
a: Your weight presses on a small spot
95204.e: With a pointed stone, your whole weight presses on a tiny point. That is why the pressure there is very great.
95204.m: On a small area the pressure is especially great.

95205.q: What do you do with a clean cloth when a wound is bleeding heavily?
a: Press it firmly on the wound
Put it next to the wound
95205.e: Pressure on the wound slows the bleeding. Then you quickly get help.
95205.m: You press a clean cloth on a bleeding wound.

95206.q: What do you feel when the phone buzzes in your trouser pocket?
95206.e: Inside the phone, a tiny motor spins very fast. The device shakes and you feel it on your skin.

95207.q: What vibrates in your throat when you hum?
95207.e: When you hum, the vocal cords in the voice box vibrate. If you put your hand on your throat, you can feel the trembling.
95207.m: When you hum, your vocal cords vibrate.

95208.q: What do you feel under your feet when a heavy lorry drives past close by?
95208.e: The heavy lorry makes the ground vibrate. You feel this vibration with your feet.
95208.m: Heavy vehicles make the ground vibrate.

95209.q: What is a device that measures the shaking of earthquakes called?
95209.e: A seismograph records even the smallest movements of the ground. In Switzerland, the Swiss Seismological Service at ETH Zurich does the measuring.

95210.q: How can deaf people feel music?
95210.e: Loud music makes the floor and the air vibrate. Deaf people feel the bass with their whole body.
95210.m: Deaf people feel music through vibrations.

95211.q: What do you feel in your fingers when you pluck a guitar string?
95211.e: The plucked string swings back and forth. This makes the note, and you feel the fine trembling.

95212.q: How does a spider notice that an insect is caught in its web?
95212.e: The trapped insect wriggles and makes the threads vibrate. The spider feels this with its legs.
95212.m: A spider feels prey by the trembling of its web.

95213.q: What do you feel in your hand with an electric toothbrush?
95213.e: In an electric toothbrush, a motor moves the brush head very fast. You feel this as a vibration in your hand.

95214.q: What do people often put in bed in winter to make it warm?
95214.e: A hot-water bottle is filled with warm water. It warms the bed and your feet.
95214.m: A hot-water bottle warms the bed.

95215.q: Which material keeps you especially warm in winter?
95215.e: There is a lot of air trapped between the wool fibres. This air holds on to your body heat.
95215.m: Wool keeps you warm in winter.

95216.q: Which T-shirt gets warmer in the sun?
95216.e: Dark colours absorb more sunlight than light ones. That is why dark clothes get warmer in the sun.
95216.m: Dark clothes get warmer in the sun.

95217.q: Why do you rub your hands together when it is cold?
95217.e: When you rub things against each other, heat is produced. This is called friction heat.

95218.q: Why do emperor penguins stand close together in winter?
95218.e: In Antarctica it is freezing cold. Huddled close together, the penguins lose less heat.

95219.q: What do you feel on your skin when you sit close to a campfire?
95219.e: The fire sends out heat rays. They warm the skin even without you touching the fire.
95219.m: A campfire warms you with heat rays.

95220.q: Why does lukewarm water feel hot on your hands after a snowball fight?
a: Because your hands are very cold
95220.e: The skin compares the temperature with its own. So cold hands feel lukewarm water as hot.
95220.m: Cold hands feel lukewarm water as hot.

95221.q: Which stove heats the living room in many old Swiss farmhouses?
95221.e: A tiled stove stores the heat of the fire in its tiles. It gives it off to the room for a long time.
95221.m: A tiled stove keeps the room warm for a long time.

95222.q: Which colour on a tap usually shows warm water?
95222.e: Red stands for warm and blue for cold. That way you know which way to turn.
95222.m: On a tap, red means warm water.

95223.q: What tickles especially when you stroke it very lightly over the skin?
95223.e: A feather touches the skin only very gently. Many people feel this light touch as tickling.
95223.m: A feather tickles on the skin.

95224.q: What does a dog do with its mouth open to cool down in the heat?
95224.e: When panting, water evaporates from the tongue and mouth. This cools the dog down.

95225.q: What is the capital of the canton of Aargau?
95225.e: Aarau is the capital of the canton of Aargau. The government and the cantonal parliament work there.

95226.q: Which river gives the canton of Aargau its name?
95226.e: The name Aargau roughly means “land on the Aare”. The Aare flows right across the whole canton.
95226.m: Aargau means land on the Aare.

95227.q: Which neighbouring country borders the canton of Aargau to the north?
95227.e: In the north, the Rhine forms the border between Aargau and Germany.
95227.m: Across the Rhine, Aargau looks towards Germany.

95228.q: Which lake is in the canton of Aargau?
95228.e: Lake Hallwil lies in the Seetal valley in the canton of Aargau. In summer you can swim and take boat trips there.
95228.m: Lake Hallwil is the largest lake in Aargau.

95229.q: Which vegetable is in the famous cake from the canton of Aargau?
95229.e: Aargau carrot cake is baked with grated carrots and almonds. It is moist and often decorated with little marzipan carrots.
95229.m: Aargau carrot cake: carrots in the cake.

95230.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Aargau?
95230.e: In the canton of Aargau, German is the official language. In everyday life people speak the Aargau dialect, in other words Swiss German.

95231.q: What is the town of Baden in the canton of Aargau known for?
a: For warm spring water to bathe in
95231.e: In Baden, warm water comes out of the ground. Even the Romans bathed there, which is why the town is called Baden, German for “bathing”.
95231.m: In Baden people bathe in warm spring water.

95232.q: How many white stars are on the coat of arms of the canton of Aargau?
95232.e: The Aargau coat of arms is divided into two halves. On the left is a white river on black, on the right three white stars on blue.
95232.m: Three stars on blue: that is Aargau.

95233.q: Which three rivers meet at the “water castle of Switzerland” in the canton of Aargau?
95233.e: Near Brugg and Windisch, the Reuss and the Limmat flow into the Aare. Because so much water comes together here, the area is called the “water castle of Switzerland”.
95233.m: The Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet at the water castle.

95234.q: What nickname does the canton of Aargau have?
95234.e: Aargau is often called the “canton of culture”. It has many castles, palaces, monasteries and museums.
95234.m: Aargau is the canton of culture.

95235.q: What is the big town festival called that is celebrated in Baden in the canton of Aargau about every ten years?
95235.e: The Badenfahrt is a huge public festival with a parade, food stalls and music. It only takes place about every ten years.
95235.m: Every ten years Baden celebrates the Badenfahrt.

95236.q: What is produced at the Riburg saltworks near Möhlin in the canton of Aargau?
95236.e: There is salt deep underground. At the Riburg saltworks it is dissolved in water, pumped up and then made into table salt and road salt.
95236.m: At Riburg, salt is brought up from deep underground.

95237.q: Which famous moated castle stands on Lake Hallwil in the canton of Aargau?
95237.e: Hallwyl Castle stands on two small islands and is surrounded by water. Today it is a museum.
95237.m: Hallwyl Castle stands in the middle of the water.

95238.q: Roughly how many people live in the canton of Aargau?
95238.e: More than 700,000 people live in Aargau. That makes it one of the most populous cantons in Switzerland.

95239.q: Which of these cantons is a neighbour of the canton of Aargau?
95239.e: Aargau borders Zurich, Zug, Lucerne, Bern, Solothurn and Basel-Landschaft. Thurgau, Glarus and Schwyz do not touch Aargau.

95240.q: What nickname does the old town of Aarau have because of its painted eaves?
95240.e: Many houses in Aarau's old town have brightly painted undersides to their roofs. That is why Aarau is called the “town of beautiful gables”.
95240.m: Aarau is the town of beautiful gables.

95246.q: Which well-known mountain is on the border of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95246.e: At 2,502 metres, the Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein. On its summit, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and St Gallen meet.
95246.m: The Säntis is the king of the Alpstein.

95247.q: Which mountain lake lies below the Ebenalp in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95247.e: The Seealpsee lies in the Alpstein. You can reach it on foot from Wasserauen.
95247.m: The Seealpsee sparkles in the Alpstein.

95248.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95248.e: The coat of arms of Appenzell Innerrhoden shows an upright black bear on a white background.
95248.m: A black bear decorates the Innerrhoden coat of arms.

95249.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95249.e: In Appenzell Innerrhoden people speak German. In everyday life you hear the typical Appenzell dialect.
95249.m: Innerrhoden speaks German with an Appenzell dialect.

95250.q: Which sweet pastry with an almond filling is a speciality from Appenzell?
95250.e: The Appenzeller Biber is a gingerbread with an almond filling. Often a picture is pressed into the dough.
95250.m: A Biber from Appenzell is gingerbread with an almond filling.

95251.q: How do people vote at the Landsgemeinde in Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95251.e: At the Landsgemeinde, the voters gather in the open air. They vote by raising their hands.
95251.m: At the Landsgemeinde, the raised hand counts.

95252.q: Which musical instrument, whose strings are struck with small hammers, belongs to Appenzell folk music?
95252.e: The hammered dulcimer (Hackbrett) is a box with many strings that you strike with two small hammers. It is part of typical Appenzell string music.
95252.m: The hammered dulcimer is heard in every Appenzell string band.

95253.q: In which part of Switzerland is the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95253.e: Appenzell Innerrhoden is in eastern Switzerland, not far from Lake Constance. Together with Ausserrhoden it is surrounded by the canton of St Gallen.

95254.q: Which canton is even smaller in area than Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95254.e: Appenzell Innerrhoden is the second-smallest canton in Switzerland. Only Basel-Stadt has an even smaller area.
95254.m: Only Basel-Stadt is smaller than Innerrhoden.

95255.q: What is the famous mountain inn called that clings to a rock face below the Ebenalp in Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95255.e: The Aescher mountain inn is built right against a steep rock face. Photos of it are famous all over the world.
95255.m: The Aescher clings to the rock below the Ebenalp.

95256.q: On which mountain in Appenzell Innerrhoden is there a revolving restaurant with a view into the Rhine Valley?
95256.e: On the Hoher Kasten, the restaurant slowly turns in a circle. So you can see into the Rhine Valley, over Lake Constance and to the mountains.
95256.m: On the Hoher Kasten the restaurant turns round.

95257.q: On which day does the Landsgemeinde in Appenzell Innerrhoden normally take place?
a: On the last Sunday in April
On the first Monday in January
95257.e: The Innerrhoden Landsgemeinde takes place every year on the last Sunday in April on the Landsgemeinde square in Appenzell.
95257.m: Last Sunday in April: Landsgemeinde in Appenzell.

95258.q: What is the mountain range in Appenzell Innerrhoden called that the Säntis and Hoher Kasten belong to?
95258.e: The Alpstein is a small, rocky mountain range in eastern Switzerland. The Säntis, the Hoher Kasten and the Ebenalp belong to it.
95258.m: The Säntis and Hoher Kasten belong to the Alpstein.

95259.q: Which state was the last of the 13 old members to join the Swiss Confederacy?
95259.e: Appenzell joined in 1513 as the 13th and last member. At that time it was still a single state; the split into Inner and Outer Rhoden came later.
95259.m: Appenzell was the 13th member of the old Confederacy.
